name: Zeri
overview: Zeri was a male Levite, specifically noted as the son of Jeduthun. He was set apart as one of the musicians chosen to prophesy using lyres, harps, and cymbals, reflecting his role in the worship ministry. Among the singers, he was the fourth chosen by lot, indicating a distinct position within the Levitical musicians.
namesAndTitles: The name Zeri means 'balsam,' a term that may evoke healing or fragrance, though the text does not elaborate on symbolic meaning. He is also referred to as Izri, which means 'YHWH designs,' highlighting a connection to divine purpose. Both names are proper names and were not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Zeri was the son of Jeduthun, a notable figure in the Levitical musical tradition. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Zeri's significance lies in his role as a designated worship leader among the Levites, chosen to prophesy musically with specific instruments. His selection by lot as the fourth among the singers underscores the organized and divinely guided nature of temple worship. Through his service, Zeri contributed to the spiritual life of Israel by facilitating prophetic worship in the house of God.
